messages:
Alyssa: Heads-up: Acme wants a short, copy-paste guide for how to allowlist traffic for our Dedicated POC. They need inbound locked down and a way for our service to hit their webhook. Any standard patterns?

Nick: We normally offer three pragmatic approaches:
1) Reserved static egress IPs for the Dedicated pool (fastest)
2) Customer-run forward proxy / outbound proxy (no inbound rule change)
3) Private connectivity (VPN/VPC peering) for completely private traffic

Alyssa: Can you draft the exact firewall entries and a brief next-steps list they can add to their security ticket?

Nick: Yep. Short versions below so they can paste.

---
Option 1 — Reserved static EIPs (recommended for POCs)
- Redwood reserves 1-4 static IPv4 addresses that our Dedicated pool will egress from.
- Customer adds those IPs to their perimeter allowlist for inbound webhooks or IP-restricted endpoints.
- We can guarantee no-change for the duration of the POC window (we commit for the reserved period).
- Next steps: Infra to allocate EIPs, exchange SOC contact, customer files firewall ticket with the EIPs.

Sample firewall lines to paste:
```
ALLOW TCP 443 FROM 203.0.113.45/32
ALLOW TCP 443 FROM 203.0.113.46/32
```
(we'll supply the real addresses once INFRA ticket is completed)

---
Option 2 — Customer forward proxy (preferred when customer forbids external inbound)
- Customer runs a proxy that accepts outbound connections from our Dedicated instances.
- Redwood configures the pool to route outbound requests through that proxy (HTTP CONNECT or TLS tunnel).
- Customer only needs to allow outbound traffic to the proxy IP and port.
- This keeps incoming connections inside their perimeter; proxy can provide audit logs.

Firewall example on customer side to allow us to reach the proxy:
```
ALLOW TCP 3128 FROM 203.0.113.0/24   # allow Redwood pool outbound
```
And proxy will forward to internal webhooks.

Operational notes: Redwood will need the proxy hostname:port and any auth headers/certs to test.

---
Option 3 — VPN or VPC peering (most segregated)
- Set up site-to-site VPN or cloud VPC peering between Acme and Redwood Private infra.
- No public egress/allowlist required; traffic flows over private path.
- Longer setup time and requires network approvals and configuration on both sides.

---
Alyssa: Good. What about source-IP-bound API keys? Acme asked if we can issue keys that only work from certain IPs.

Nick: We don't currently support issuing API keys restricted by source IP on the hosted API. For Dedicated, the usual control is network-level allowlisting (customer firewall) combined with reserved EIPs. If they need token-level scoping we can discuss a short-term gated feature but it needs eng review and ETA.

Alyssa: They also asked for an SLA note about the EIPs during the POC (so SOC can sign off).

Nick: For POCs we can mark the EIPs as "reserved" for the agreed window and note that we will not rotate them during that window. I'll add that to the infra ticket and we can produce a short written confirmation if legal needs it.

Alyssa: Can we include a tiny connectivity test they can run once we provide IPs?

Nick: Sure — two quick checks:
1) Redwood-initiated webhook test (we run this against a customer test endpoint):
```
# Redwood will run this from the Dedicated pool once EIPs are active
curl -v -X POST 'https://acme.example.com/redwood-test' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"ping":"ok"}'
```
2) If there is a proxy, simple proxy curl from our instance:
```
# from our Dedicated instance via the customer's proxy
curl -x http://proxy.acme.example.com:3128 -v https://internal.acme.example.com/health
```

InfraBot: INFRA-7890 created: Reserve 2 EIPs for "dedicated-poc-acme". Requester: @Nick. ETA: 48 hours.

Jordan: Actions:
- Nick: follow up when INFRA-7890 has IPs and paste them here. Add the no-rotation pledge for the POC window.
- Alyssa: send the three-option note to Acme, ask which approach they prefer and request SOC contact.
- Jordan: include a line item in the quote for reserved EIPs (nominal monthly fee for the POC).

Maya: I can help run a 15-min networking handoff with Acme SOC once we have IPs or proxy details. Happy to join.

Nick: If they pick the proxy approach, I'll coordinate the proxy config and provide a brief test script for auth headers and TLS validation.

Alyssa: I'll message Acme and paste the firewall snippets. Will update here when they answer. :slightly_smiling_face:
